answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each agent to a Wesolowski VDF: a long chain of sequential modular squarings whose output is checked with a succinct proof. Because each square depends on the previous result, an attacker simulating multiple clones cannot parallelize one identity’s computation across GPUs; every clone faces the same wall-clock delay, limiting Sybil growth at the horizon despite attempts to wander across hardware, while the falcon verifier stays efficient.
